title: Kafka: fintech risk pipeline
tagline: Payments flow through Kafka into TiDB, and every committed change flows back out through TiCDC.
pattern: fintech risk pipeline: payment events stream through Kafka into TiDB, risk state lives in TiDB, and TiCDC streams every change back out to Kafka for downstream consumers

metrics.label: Produce rate
metrics.howMeasured: Acked messages per tick from the producer's Kafka client, divided by tick seconds.

metrics.label: Ingest rate
metrics.howMeasured: affectedRows from the batched upsert per tick, divided by tick seconds.

metrics.label: Ingester consumer lag
metrics.howMeasured: High-water mark minus committed offset for the ingester's consumer group on payments, summed across partitions via the Kafka admin client.

metrics.label: Risk consumer lag
metrics.howMeasured: High-water mark minus committed offset for the risk consumer's group on tidb-changes.

metrics.label: TiDB upsert p99
metrics.howMeasured: summarize() over per-batch upsert wall-clock times measured with timed(), emitted once per tick.

metrics.label: TiCDC checkpoint lag
metrics.howMeasured: now minus Date.parse(checkpoint_time) from GET /api/v2/changefeeds/{id} on the local TiCDC OpenAPI v2.

metrics.label: End-to-end latency p50
metrics.howMeasured: p50 of (CDC event consumed at) minus (produce_ts embedded in the payment payload), over the tick's samples.

metrics.label: End-to-end latency p99
metrics.howMeasured: p99 of the same sample set as e2e-latency-p50.

metrics.label: Duplicate CDC events observed
metrics.howMeasured: Cumulative count of (payment_id, commit_ts) pairs seen more than once on tidb-changes, tracked by the risk consumer's dedupe set.

phases.label: Warming up
phases.narration: We're standing up a normal Kafka-to-TiDB pipeline: nothing custom, just a consumer doing upserts.

phases.label: Steady state
phases.narration: At steady state every payment event becomes a row in TiDB, and TiCDC re-publishes that row change within milliseconds.

phases.label: 10x burst
phases.narration: Now we 10x the load. Watch ingest rate and TiCDC checkpoint lag - TiDB absorbs it, TiCDC catches up.

phases.label: Ingester restart
phases.narration: We kill the ingester consumer. Kafka holds its committed offset, so when it reconnects it resumes exactly where it left off - no loss, no duplicate rows in TiDB.

phases.label: Pause and resume the changefeed
phases.narration: We pause the changefeed itself. TiDB keeps taking writes. When we resume, TiCDC catches up from its checkpoint - and this is exactly where Kafka's at-least-once delivery shows up as visible duplicates downstream.

phases.label: Wrap-up
phases.narration: Produced count equals rows in TiDB equals distinct CDC events. Duplicates happened, and we caught every one of them.

checks.label: Produced count equals TiDB row count
checks.description: Producer's cumulative event count equals SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments once the producer is idle.

checks.label: TiDB rows equal distinct CDC events
checks.description: Count of distinct (payment_id, commit_ts) pairs seen on tidb-changes equals the TiDB row count.

checks.label: Zero duplicate rows in TiDB
checks.description: SELECT payment_id, COUNT(*) FROM payments GROUP BY payment_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 returns no rows.

controls.label: Burst 10x for 30s
controls.description: Multiplies producer rate by 10 for 30 seconds, then returns to baseline.

controls.label: Kill ingester
controls.description: Tears down and recreates the ingester's Kafka consumer under the same group id.
